item.title: Lindsey Buckingham Says He & Stevie Nicks Are ‘Talking All the Time Now’ After Fleetwood Mac Fallout
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Welcome to "Trending on Billboard"! Today, we're talking about Fleetwood Mac and the latest update on their iconic journey. Lindsey Buckingham, the band's guitarist, recently sat down with E! News to discuss the band's upcoming documentary and his relationship with his bandmates, particularly Stevie Nicks.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: Buckingham shared that working on the documentary has been a "very circular healing process" for the band, helping them to move forward from their past rifts. You might remember that Buckingham was temporarily fired from the lineup back in 2019, but it seems that those wounds have now been healed.
[Short music transition]
Host: In fact, Buckingham revealed that he and Stevie Nicks are now talking all the time, which is a big step forward considering their famously fraught relationship over the decades. The two even teamed up last year to re-release their 1973 album, Buckingham Nicks, which reached No. 3 on the Top Album Sales chart.
[Soft music continues]
Host: The Fleetwood Mac documentary, directed by Frank Marshall, is expected to arrive in 2027, although no official release date has been announced. Buckingham hinted that next year will be an interesting one, with several projects in the works. As he put it, "I think quite a few things will reveal themselves."
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's all for today's update on Fleetwood Mac. It's great to see the band moving forward and healing their past wounds. We can't wait to see what's in store for them in the future. Thanks for tuning in to "Trending on Billboard"!
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
